title: A model of the message queue
hints: Keep each window's procedure in a `std::shared_ptr`, and copy the pointer before calling it: a window that destroys itself from inside its own procedure must not destroy the function that is still running.
For the timer, compare each timer's next time with the clock, pick the earliest due one, and set its next time from *now*, not from its old time: that is what makes missed ticks combine.
requirements: Posted messages come out in order, before a requested quit, before paint and timer messages.
`WM_PAINT` repeats until the window is validated, and several invalidations give one paint.
Timer ticks missed while busy combine into one.
Destroying a window sends `WM_DESTROY` and throws away its pending messages; a window may destroy itself from inside its own procedure.
stretch: Add `SendMessage` across "threads" (two queues, where sending to the other thread's window waits until that thread's loop handles it) and show how two threads sending to each other at the same time deadlock.
